Campaign brief: Resend gives a small product team a separate, developer-controlled route for authentication and other transactional email through SMTP or SDKs, with paid plans removing Resend’s daily sending limit when the Free plan’s 100-per-day ceiling is no longer sufficient.
events.reader:
Selected audience: The one backend engineer at a ten-person product team who owns email because nobody else does.
Situation context (grounded; check applicability): Individual engineers integrating a hosted auth platform (Supabase Auth) into a product's signup, password-reset, invite, and OTP flows post first-person accounts, in GitHub issues and discussions on the platform's own repos, of hitting the built-in email rate limit and having to reason through Supabase's dashboard logs, SMTP settings, and plan tiers themselves to diagnose it.
events.reader_segment: The one backend engineer at a ten-person product team who owns email because nobody else does
events.promise: Resend gives a small product team a separate, developer-controlled route for authentication and other transactional email through SMTP or SDKs, with paid plans removing Resend’s daily sending limit when the Free plan’s 100-per-day ceiling is no longer sufficient.
events.arc: Move from recognition of the built-in sender ceiling, to the announcement that a separately configured sending route is available, to its exact limits and a bounded proof point, then invite the reader to evaluate the route without implying that Resend changes the auth platform’s own settings.

emails.job: Get a problem-aware backend engineer to consider Resend as the separate sending route behind authentication email and begin a bounded self-serve evaluation.
emails.single_idea: Resend is now available as a developer-controlled route for authentication and other transactional email: connect through SMTP or an official SDK, start within a clearly stated Free-plan limit, and move to a paid plan with no daily sending limit when volume requires it.
emails.objection: Switching sending providers could become a larger project than this small team has time to take on.
must_not_say: Resend automatically raises or removes the hosted-auth platform’s own rate limit; that setting still has to be changed there.
Resend detects, prevents, or survives an upstream dashboard action that clears SMTP configuration.
Resend explains how another platform counts sends against its rate limit.
The Free plan is uncapped; it is limited to 100 emails per day.
Transactional and marketing sending are automatically isolated by provider, account, domain, or infrastructure; both can live on Resend, and IP isolation requires an eligible Scale-plan dedicated IP.
A complete migration, authentication integration, or production rollout takes 30 minutes; the evidence covers only Raycast’s small waitlist-email test.
Guaranteed inbox placement, guaranteed deliverability, or superiority on speed, breadth, quality, control, effort, or security.

Resend is a separate provider, not a change to the auth platform's own limiter: the platform's dashboard rate limit still has to be raised by hand after wiring SMTP, and Resend's own free tier reimposes a 100-emails-a-day cap.

Only the paid tiers remove the daily cap; on the free plan the engineer swaps one 100/day ceiling for another, and nothing in the ledger speaks to the auth platform's own rate-limit setting that still has to be raised.
emails.felt_need: Auth email sending (signup confirmation, OTP, magic link, invites) gets blocked with a 429 email rate limit error under normal usage, even when the reporter believes they are under the documented limit.
emails.status_quo: Checks the platform's own Auth logs in the dashboard to verify whether the documented email limit was actually exceeded.
emails.why_it_fails: Upgrading the hosted-auth subscription does not itself raise that platform’s built-in email limit. Using a separate SMTP provider and adjusting the auth platform’s own rate-limit setting are separate steps.
emails.mechanism: Resend provides SMTP and official SDK integration paths. Its Free plan is capped at 100 emails per day, while Pro, Scale, and Enterprise have no daily Resend limit. Use Raycast’s documented 30-minute waitlist-email test only to show that a first evaluation can be narrow—not as proof of a complete authentication migration.
emails.next_step_decision: Decide whether to run a limited Resend evaluation using the integration path that fits the current backend before committing to a paid plan or broader migration.
emails.next_step_value: A free account provides a bounded starting point for evaluating Resend’s SMTP or SDK route, with the 100-email-per-day Free limit stated upfront.
emails.next_step_limit: Signing up does not change the hosted-auth platform’s rate-limit setting, validate its SMTP configuration, prove production deliverability, or establish the effort of a complete migration.

alternative_arguments.single_idea: Resend offers a more maintainable way to manage transactional-email content while keeping templates close to the development workflow.
alternative_arguments.felt_need: Auth email sending (signup confirmation, OTP, magic link, invites) gets blocked with a 429 email rate limit error under normal usage, even when the reporter believes they are under the documented limit.
alternative_arguments.status_quo: Checks the platform's own Auth logs in the dashboard to verify whether the documented email limit was actually exceeded.
alternative_arguments.why_it_fails: As more messages and contributors are added, ad hoc template changes lack a dedicated publish flow and revision history.
alternative_arguments.mechanism: Templates can be built with React Email, managed with auto-save and revision history, and sent using a template ID plus variables.
alternative_arguments.belief_shift: Before: adopting an email platform means handing over the entire email program or rewriting content outside the code workflow. After: one transactional template can be evaluated while content remains in React and the API call is reduced to a template ID and variables.
must_not_say: Resend fully outsources the transactional-email program.
Templates provide a one-click migration from the reader’s current system.
Using Templates eliminates all engineering ownership or maintenance.
This template workflow fixes hosted-auth rate limits or upstream SMTP configuration failures.

The researched poster explicitly refuses to fully outsource the program, so only parts move: content stays in their own components, observability is bounded by 30-day data retention, and automation runs bill at $0.0015 each once the free.
alternative_arguments.objection: I do not want to hand over the whole email program or replace every template at once.
alternative_arguments.next_step_decision: Decide whether one authentication-email template is a suitable pilot for Resend’s React Email and template-ID workflow.
alternative_arguments.next_step_value: The documentation lets the reader inspect how React Email templates are built and how a published template is called with an ID and variables.
alternative_arguments.next_step_limit: Reviewing the template workflow does not establish the effort of migrating the full email system, compatibility with a specific hosted-auth setup, or production delivery performance.
alternative_arguments.subject_strategy: Frame the product launch around taming transactional-template growth while preserving a developer-owned React workflow; avoid broad claims about simplicity or replacing the entire system.

events.body:
Resend is now available as a separate route for authentication and other transactional email. Use it for signup confirmations, password resets, invites, and OTP flows when a hosted sender’s built-in ceiling no longer fits.

Connect through SMTP or an official SDK. Configuring Resend does not change your authentication platform’s rate-limit setting; that setting must be adjusted separately after wiring SMTP.

A first evaluation can stay narrow. Raycast tested Resend with waitlist emails for its iOS and Windows apps and completed that test within 30 minutes.

The Free plan includes SMTP relay and official SDKs, with a **100-email-per-day** limit. Pro, Scale, and Enterprise plans have **no daily Resend limit**.

Sign up for free

- the Resend engineering team

events.body:
Checking Auth logs can confirm why an email was blocked. It still leaves template changes to be published and tracked as the number of messages and contributors grows.

Resend is now available. It is an email-sending platform for developers, connecting authentication and other transactional flows through SMTP or official SDKs.

Build templates with React Email, then manage them with auto-save and full revision history. When a version is published, send it with a template ID and variables.

You do not need to replace every message to evaluate the workflow. Start with one authentication email and inspect how the template is built and called.

Read the documentation.

Campaign brief: Resend gives this engineer a separate, developer-oriented route for transactional email through SMTP or official SDKs when a hosted platform's built-in sender is no longer sufficient.
events.reader:
Selected audience: The one backend engineer at a ten-person product team who owns email because nobody else does.
Situation context (inferred; check applicability): The single engineer at a small product team who shipped auth, billing and notifications and therefore inherited email; visible in auth-platform issue threads asking why confirmation mail stopped at four an hour, and in provider-choice threads where the criterion is 'start sending on day 0 once you verify your domain'

events.promise: Resend gives this engineer a separate, developer-oriented route for transactional email through SMTP or official SDKs when a hosted platform's built-in sender is no longer sufficient.
events.arc: Recognize the production decision hidden inside the auth email limit, announce Resend as the available alternative route, substantiate the practical path with plan limits and a narrowly scoped customer example, then invite one controlled test.

emails.job: Announce Resend as an available route for auth-critical transactional email and earn a free signup to test one flow.
emails.single_idea: Before launch traffic makes a hosted auth platform's built-in sender a constraint, the engineer can route transactional email through Resend using SMTP or an official SDK; paid Resend plans have no daily sending limit, while Free provides a bounded starting point at 100 emails per day.
emails.objection: Changing the sending route before launch sounds like a migration project the engineer does not have time to absorb.
must_not_say: Do not claim Resend changes, explains, or automatically raises the hosted auth platform's own rate-limit setting.
Do not claim Resend detects or prevents the upstream dashboard behavior that can erase SMTP configuration.
Do not imply that the Free plan removes sending ceilings; it is limited to 100 emails per day.
Do not promise guaranteed delivery, inbox placement, uninterrupted auth email, or the elimination of 429 errors across the full integration.

Do not claim transactional and marketing traffic are isolated at the account or infrastructure level; dedicated-IP isolation is limited to eligible Scale customers sending more than 3,000 emails per day.
Do not turn Raycast's 30-minute waitlist-email test into a claim that a complete migration takes 30 minutes.
Do not broaden the email into security, compliance, dedicated IPs, Automations, Broadcasts, enterprise support, or the full feature list.
Do not present Resend as fixing opaque metering or silent configuration failures inside another vendor's platform.
emails.felt_need: Auth email sending (signup confirmation, OTP, magic link, invites) gets blocked with a 429 email rate limit error under normal usage, even when the reporter believes they are under the documented limit.
emails.status_quo: Checks the platform's own Auth logs in the dashboard to verify whether the documented email limit was actually exceeded.
emails.why_it_fails: The built-in sender remains its own ceiling, and upgrading the hosted platform's subscription does not itself replace that sender; configuring custom SMTP and adjusting the platform's separate rate-limit setting are still required.
emails.mechanism: Resend supplies a separate sending route through SMTP and official SDKs. Its Free plan is capped at 100 emails per day, while Pro, Scale, and Enterprise have no daily sending limit.
emails.next_step_decision: Decide whether Resend is a viable sending route for one auth-critical transactional flow before adopting it more broadly.
emails.next_step_value: Create an account, verify a domain, obtain an API key, and assess an SMTP or SDK path within the Free plan's 100-email daily ceiling.
emails.next_step_limit: This step does not raise the hosted auth platform's separate rate-limit setting, establish production deliverability, or remove the Free plan's 100-email daily cap.

alternative_arguments.single_idea: Resend can be evaluated without risking real customer email: test mode simulates delivered, bounced, and spam-complaint events before the team moves a production flow.
alternative_arguments.felt_need: Auth email sending (signup confirmation, OTP, magic link, invites) gets blocked with a 429 email rate limit error under normal usage, even when the reporter believes they are under the documented limit.
alternative_arguments.status_quo: Checks the platform's own Auth logs in the dashboard to verify whether the documented email limit was actually exceeded.
alternative_arguments.why_it_fails: That tests the hosted platform's current path rather than Resend's events, dashboard, webhooks, and API behavior.
alternative_arguments.mechanism: Resend test mode simulates email events without sending real messages to real recipients or affecting domain reputation.
alternative_arguments.belief_shift: Before: evaluating another provider requires putting a real auth flow or real recipients at risk. After: Resend provides a contained simulation step that can precede any production decision.
must_not_say: Do not claim simulation proves production delivery, inbox placement, SMTP compatibility, or end-to-end behavior inside the hosted auth platform.
Do not describe Raycast's 30-minute waitlist-email test as a complete migration.
Do not claim test mode detects or prevents upstream SMTP configuration resets.
alternative_arguments.objection: Testing another provider could accidentally send real email or create more production risk.
alternative_arguments.next_step_decision: Decide whether Resend's event handling and developer workflow justify testing one real transactional flow.
alternative_arguments.next_step_value: Create an account and use test mode to simulate delivery, bounce, and spam-complaint events before sending to real recipients.
alternative_arguments.next_step_limit: The simulation does not validate production deliverability, the hosted platform's SMTP integration, or its separate rate-limit configuration.
alternative_arguments.subject_strategy: Lead with the availability of a risk-contained way to test a new transactional email route, without promising a migration or production outcome.

events.body:
Resend gives you a separate route for transactional email through SMTP or an official SDK. Your auth platform can handle authentication without its built-in sender remaining the only route for confirmations, OTPs, magic links, or invites.

When a built-in sender reaches its limit, retrying or upgrading the platform plan does not replace that sender. Custom SMTP and the platform’s separate rate-limit settings still need to be configured where applicable.

You can evaluate Resend without moving every email flow. Create an account, verify your domain, obtain an API key, and test one auth-critical message through SMTP or the SDK for your stack.

The Free plan has a **100-email daily limit**. Pro, Scale, and Enterprise plans have **no daily sending limit**, giving you a defined starting point before deciding whether to adopt Resend more broadly.

events.body:
Resend test mode lets you simulate email events without sending real messages to real recipients. Use test addresses for delivered, bounced, and spam-complaint events.

Introducing Resend: an email-sending platform for developers to send transactional email through SMTP or official SDKs. Test mode gives you access to the Dashboard, Webhooks, and API without affecting domain reputation.

That creates a contained first step before putting signup confirmations, OTPs, magic links, or invitations on a new route. You can inspect event handling before deciding whether to test one real transactional flow.

The simulation does not validate production deliverability, a hosted platform’s SMTP integration, or its separate rate-limit configuration. Those remain production checks.

Create a free account, then use test mode to see how Resend handles the three simulated outcomes.
